## Results and scope

The manual and package chain-ladder calculations both estimate
**$`r millions(cl_total)` million** of unpaid losses through development age 10.
The original reserve discrepancy is fully reconciled. The two BF calculations
below show how the result changes when the expected loss ratio (ELR) changes.
Neither ELR is an independent prior.

```{r report-headline, results='asis'}
view <- headline
names(view) <- c("Calculation", "Unpaid (USD millions)")
view[[2]] <- millions(view[[2]])
knitr::kable(view, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "r"))
```

Mack's standard error is **$`r millions(mack_se)` million**, with a coefficient
of variation of **`r percent(mack_cv)`**. These apply to the common-basis estimate
above. They are conditional on the model and exclude development beyond age 10.

### The book and valuation

The source is the CAS Schedule P workers' compensation dataset. Code 388 is
labelled **Federal Ins Co Grp**, with `Single = 0`, identifying an insurer group.
The actual file has `r nrow(co)` records for this group, covering accident years
`r min(reserve_tbl$acc_year)`-`r max(reserve_tbl$acc_year)` and ten development lags.
Accident year 2007 is absent for this group; no row was invented to fill it.

Only observations with accident year + development lag - 1 at or before 2007
enter the fitted triangle. There are `r data_audit$observed_cells` such observations;
`r data_audit$excluded_future_cells` later observations are excluded. This is a
historical portfolio study, not a current reserve recommendation.

### What the estimates mean

The paid-loss measure includes allocated expenses and is net of reinsurance.
Net earned premium is used for the ELR calculations. All source monetary values
are interpreted as USD thousands; report and chart totals use USD millions.
The estimates cover future payments on reported and unreported claims. This is
**unpaid losses**, not solely incurred-but-not-reported claims. The package's
`IBNR` output field is used as an unpaid-loss quantity in this paid triangle.

“Ultimate” in the calculation means projected cumulative paid at age 10.
No later development is assumed. It does not establish that all claims are settled.

\newpage

## Why the original reserves differed

The manual calculation used development ages 1-10. The old Mack input used
ages 1-9, dropping the sole observed age-10 payment. This changed both the
projection horizon and the latest paid amount for accident year 1998.

```{r reconciliation-summary, results='asis'}
view <- basis_table
view[-1] <- lapply(view[-1], millions)
names(view) <- c("Basis", "Latest paid", "Projected paid", "Unpaid")
knitr::kable(view, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = "lrrr")
```

All amounts above are USD millions. The reduction in projected paid losses was
$`r millions(ultimate_gap)` million, partly offset by a $`r millions(paid_gap)` million
reduction in latest paid. Since unpaid = projected paid - latest paid, the net
difference is **$`r millions(reserve_gap)` million**, or
**`r percent(reserve_gap / cl_total)`** of the manual estimate. It was not immaterial.

### The final observed development factor

The age-9-to-10 factor is `r fmt(tail(ldfs$ldf_vw, 1), 9)`, based only on the 1998
pair: `r fmt(tri_mat['1998','10'], 0)` / `r fmt(tri_mat['1998','9'], 0)` in USD thousands.
Dropping it removes a roughly `r percent(tail(ldfs$ldf_vw,1)-1)` multiplier from the
age-9 projected totals. Its impact accumulates across accident years.

```{r reconciliation-years, results='asis'}
view <- reconciliation
view[-1] <- lapply(view[-1], millions)
names(view) <- c("Accident year", "Latest paid change", "Projected change", "Unpaid change")
knitr::kable(view, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = "rrrr")
```

Changes are full-horizon minus original trimmed estimates, in USD millions.

### Common-basis comparison

The installed ChainLadder version is `r as.character(packageVersion('ChainLadder'))`.
Its standard Mack input supports at least as many origin rows as development
columns; a square shape is not universally required. The original 9-by-10 input
is rejected directly. The documentation also describes other rectangular cases.

For this book, using ages **2-10** gives a standard 9-by-9 triangle. Every origin
has already reached age 2, so the unused age-1-to-2 factor is omitted while all
latest payments and needed factors are retained. Volume weighting (`alpha = 1`),
accident years, and the no-tail assumption are unchanged. Manual and package
latest paid, projected paid and unpaid losses agree by origin within
`1e-7` in USD thousands. No unexplained reserve difference remains.

\newpage

## Bornhuetter-Ferguson sensitivities

For paid-loss development, the BF estimate is:

\[
\text{Unpaid}_i = \text{Premium}_i \times \text{ELR} \times (1 - 1/\text{CDF}_i).
\]

The original ELR uses observed paid losses divided by net earned premium for
years with CDF below 1.05. Those years are
**`r paste(mature$acc_year, collapse = ', ')`**, not just 1998-1999. This gives
**`r percent(elr, 6)`**. A low CDF does not prove settlement or make this an
external expectation.

The second scenario uses total CL projected losses divided by total net earned
premium: **`r percent(cl_implied_elr, 6)`**. It is labelled **CL-implied ELR sensitivity**.
The computation uses full precision; 40.0% was a rounded display label.

```{r bf-scenarios-table, results='asis'}
view <- data.frame(Scenario = c("Mature-year paid ELR", "CL-implied ELR", "Exactly 40% (rounding check)"),
                   ELR = percent(bf_scenarios$ELR, 6),
                   Unpaid = millions(bf_scenarios$unpaid_000s))
names(view)[3] <- "Unpaid (USD millions)"
knitr::kable(view, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = "lrr")
```

```{r sensitivity-chart, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath("figures/cl_vs_bf_sensitivity.png"), rel_path = FALSE)
```

**Interpretation.** The difference follows from the ELR inputs applied to the
same premiums and unpaid proportions. The CL-implied scenario reuses CL results,
so its proximity to CL is not independent validation. Neither scenario is
labelled “correct,” “conservative,” or a preferred reserve based only on proximity.

\newpage

## Uncertainty on the common basis

```{r uncertainty-chart, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath("figures/unpaid_by_accident_year.png"), rel_path = FALSE)
```

```{r year-results, results='asis'}
view <- by_year[c("Accident_year", "Age", "CDF", "Unpaid_000s", "Mack_SE_000s")]
view$CDF <- fmt(view$CDF, 3)
view$Unpaid_000s <- millions(view$Unpaid_000s)
view$Mack_SE_000s <- millions(view$Mack_SE_000s)
names(view) <- c("Accident year", "Latest age", "CDF", "Unpaid (millions)", "SE (millions)")
knitr::kable(view, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = "rrrrr")
```

Mack standard errors estimate prediction uncertainty under chain-ladder
conditional mean and variance assumptions and independence between accident
years. They include process and parameter risk within the selected model.
The total SE includes dependence from shared factor estimates; it is not the
sum of the per-year SEs. The plotted one-SE bands are not confidence intervals.

The final development factor has only one observed pair, so the final variance
uses the package's `est.sigma = "Mack"` approximation. Arithmetic agreement does
not establish the model assumptions. The old roughly 16% CV described the
trimmed-age-9 calculation; it cannot be attached to the age-10 reserve. The
common-basis CV is `r percent(mack_cv)`.

\newpage

## Data checks and limits

```{r audit-table, results='asis'}
knitr::kable(audit_summary, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = "lr")
```

The code checks required numeric fields and finite values, integer years and
lags, unique company/year/lag keys, expected observed cells through the valuation
date, and numeric column ordering. Each accident year's premium must agree
across development lags. Direct and assumed premium less ceded premium must
equal net earned premium. Non-positive paired development denominators stop
the analysis for investigation instead of causing observations to be dropped.

### The 2001 paid-loss decrease

Cumulative paid for accident year 2001 decreases from
$`r millions(tri_mat['2001','6'])` million at age 6 to
$`r millions(tri_mat['2001','7'])` million at age 7: a
**$`r millions(abs(data_audit$negative_increments$increment[1]))` million decrease**.
The original “smooth development” description was unsupported.

The supplied file matches the official CAS download byte for byte, and the
decrease is present in the official records. The CSV does not explain its cause
or provide transaction details to resolve it. It is retained in the factors and
flagged in every run. No recovery, correction or other economic explanation is
asserted without evidence. Resolving the cause would require underlying filings
or clarification from the data provider.

### Limits of the analysis

- **Tail:** projected paid at age 10 is treated as ultimate. The dataset does not
  establish that payments beyond this horizon are zero. The Mack SE excludes
  uncertainty about omitted later development.
- **Model:** stability of development and independence across origin years have
  not been established by the synthetic tests. Calendar effects, business mix,
  reinsurance changes and other model misspecification are not quantified here.
- **ELRs:** both BF scenarios use this book's own experience. Neither supplies
  independent evidence about expected losses.
- **Coverage:** the selected group's 2007 accident year is not present. The
  supplied posted-reserve field is not used as a benchmark because its coverage
  is not established as matching this paid-loss projection.
- **Validation:** later observations exist, but no runoff backtest is implemented.
  No predictive validation, credibility ranking or reserve recommendation is claimed.

\newpage

## Reproduction and sources

From the repository root, run:

```sh
Rscript build.R
```

The RStudio Console equivalent is `source("build.R")`. It launches a fresh R
process, restores the recorded package environment, runs `r test_groups` synthetic
test groups, and generates the CSV tables, three figures, README and this PDF.
Both document sources read the same objects generated by the current analysis.
No headline result is maintained separately by hand.

### Environment and files

The recorded R version is `r getRversion()`. ChainLadder is
`r as.character(packageVersion('ChainLadder'))`; renv is
`r as.character(packageVersion('renv'))`. The lockfile records package versions
and sources. Pandoc and a LaTeX distribution are external prerequisites;
renv does not install or pin their complete system environments. Local build
versions and session details are saved under `outputs/`.

The editable sources are `report/report.Rmd` and `report/README.Rmd`. The shared
calculation functions are in `R/reserving.R`; the main analysis is
`wc_loss_reserving.R`. Tests use synthetic data and can run without the CAS CSV.
Tables and detailed input checks are regenerated under `outputs/tables/`, which
is kept local. Only the intended report, charts, source and environment files
are prepared for repository review.

### Data acquisition

Download `wkcomp_pos_98-07.csv` from the CAS page's current workers' compensation
link and place it at the repository root. The earlier 2011 release is a different
file and schema. Read the usage terms and attribution requirements. The source
CSV is not redistributed. The build checks its SHA-256 against the reference
release so a changed input cannot silently reuse the report's scope statements.

Reference SHA-256:

```{r checksum, results='asis'}
cat(paste0("\\begin{small}\\begin{verbatim}\n", substr(input_sha256,1,32), "\n", substr(input_sha256,33,64), "\n\\end{verbatim}\\end{small}\n"))
```
